links.outcome: Overconfident assertions in patient-facing LLM answers after medical fine-tuning
links.effect: Continued-pretraining medical models (BioMistral, OpenBioLLM) consistently amplified overconfident assertions; Med42 instruction-tuning did not. Risk-bearing language was independent of hallucination rate (Spearman rho = -0.065, n = 300).
links.quote: Second, medical fine-tuning does not reduce aggregate risk but reshapes it: continued-pretraining adaptations (BioMistral, OpenBioLLM) consistently suppress high-alert medication mentions while amplifying overconfident assertions, whereas clinical instruction-tuning (Med42) suppresses dosing only, without amplifying overconfidence.

unlisted_practices: Risk-sensitive rubric evaluation of risk-bearing language (directives, dosing, triage cues, high-alert medications, overconfidence) beyond factuality
Three-judge LLM ensemble for severity classification with inter-rater reliability checks
Comparing general versus medically fine-tuned LLMs on risk profiles

screen.reason: Empirical benchmarking study evaluating general vs. medically fine-tuned LLMs on patient-facing medical question answering using an LLM-judge safety evaluation framework to detect risk-bearing language.
